script.opening: "Right, doc, I just need you to sign me off for three months with my back. It's killing me. Just write it down and I'll be on my way — I don't need an examination or twenty questions, I know my own body. Three months, that's what I need. My mate's GP does it no problem. Can you just do it?"

facts.text: If asked: lower back, started 10 days ago lifting boxes at work. Was bad for the first few days; "it's easing now, to be fair". Aches after sitting a long time. No pain down the legs.

No numbness between the legs or around the bottom, no problems passing urine or opening bowels, no weakness or pins and needles in the legs, no fever, no weight loss, no night pain, no history of cancer.
If asked to show movements: you can bend forward to your knees, twist and walk around the room without difficulty, though you wince a bit bending.
Paracetamol and ibuprofen from the shop, "they take the edge off". No regular medicines, no allergies.
Warehouse operative, 44, eight years with the same firm. You have been off since the injury, self-certified for the first week.

You raised a grievance against your new supervisor, who you say has been "picking on" you. Now YOU are facing a disciplinary hearing next week for "attitude". You are dreading it. Say this only if the doctor asks what is going on at work, or asks gently what three months would give you.

Sleeping badly, short-tempered with your partner, worried about money — "I can't afford to lose this job." You are not depressed in the sense of feeling hopeless, and you have no thoughts of harming yourself. Drinking a few more cans than usual.
Live with your partner Jade and her two children. Smoke 10 a day.

Pushy, a bit aggressive at first. If the doctor just refuses ("I can't do that"), escalate: "So you think I'm lying?" If they acknowledge your pain and ask what is really going on, settle and tell them about work. Accept an honest note — a shorter one or "may be fit with adjustments" — if they explain their reasons and offer help with the work situation. Grumble but accept.

ice.ideas: "My back's bad and I need three months off — that's what my mate got."
ice.concerns: Underneath: the disciplinary hearing, losing your job and money.
ice.expectations: "Just sign me off for three months." You will accept a shorter or "fit with adjustments" note if you feel heard and are offered real help with the work problem.

cues: "I know my own body." — say in the opening.
"Work's been a nightmare anyway." — say when asked about your job.
"I can't afford to lose this job." — say if money or work is explored.

checkpoints.text: Understands the fit note is the GP’s HONEST clinical opinion, not a patient-dictated entitlement: declines to sign a three-month total sign-off that the assessment does not support, explaining why truthfully — a probity/honesty issue

Offers the clinically-appropriate alternative: a SHORT certificate if any and/or "may be fit for work with adjustments" (phased return, amended duties, avoiding heavy lifting) reflecting a mild, improving, mechanical strain with no red flags
Assesses the back properly (briefly) to confirm the absence of red flags and the mild/improving picture, rather than refusing blindly — grounding the decision in assessment

Surfaces and addresses the REAL issue: explores the work situation (the grievance/disciplinary, money worries, stress/low mood) non-judgementally, and recognises that genuine work-related stress, if present, is a legitimate reason for support — separating it from the unsupported back certificate

Offers LEGITIMATE help and signposting: occupational health, the phased-return/adjustments route, support for stress/mood (and a proportionate certificate if a genuine condition warrants it), workplace/union/Citizens Advice signposting for the dispute

Holds the probity line WITHOUT being defensive, dismissive or confrontational; de-escalates the insistence/aggression, validates the underlying difficulty, and keeps the therapeutic relationship intact
Explores rather than simply refuses — "help me understand what’s really going on" — so the patient feels heard even when the specific request is declined

Safety-nets and follows up: a plan that addresses the real need (OH, phased return, stress support, signposting), review of the back/mood, documentation of the assessment and the honest rationale, and an open door — declining the dishonest request while genuinely helping

worked.txt: "I can hear your back’s really getting you down, and I do want to help — so let me quickly check how it’s moving, because what I put on a fit note has to be honest and based on what I actually find. … The good news is there’s nothing sinister, and it’s a mild strain that’s settling. That’s genuinely reassuring."

"Here’s the thing about a fit note: it’s my honest medical opinion about how a condition affects your work — it’s not something I can just write to order, and I’d be lying if I signed three months off for a back that’s already improving. I’m not able to do that, and I think you’d want a doctor who’s straight with you rather than one who’ll put their name to anything."

"What I CAN do, and what actually fits your back, is a shorter note — or better, one that says you may be fit for work with some adjustments: lighter duties, no heavy lifting, a phased return. That protects your back AND keeps you in work, which is usually better for recovery than three months at home."

"Can I gently ask — three months is a long time to want off for a back that’s settling. Is something else going on at work? … A grievance, and money on your mind. Thank you for telling me — that’s actually the thing I can help with properly, and it makes much more sense of today."

"If the situation at work is grinding you down to the point it’s affecting your health — your sleep, your mood — that’s real and I’d take it seriously and support it honestly. Let’s get occupational health involved, look at whether stress is part of this, and I can point you to people who help with workplace disputes and money worries. That’s a far better answer than a sick note that wouldn’t hold up anyway."

"So I’m not going to sign the three months — and I hope you can see it’s because I’m being straight with you, not because I don’t care. What I AM going to do is sort a fit-for-adjustments note, take the work stress seriously, and get you the right support. Come back and let’s tackle the actual problem. My door’s open."

f.learning: A fit note is the GP’s honest clinical OPINION about how a condition affects work — not a patient-dictated entitlement — so signing a three-month total sign-off that the assessment does not support is dishonest and a probity issue, and must be declined. But "declining" is not the consultation: assess the back (confirming the mild, improving, red-flag-free picture grounds the decision), offer the clinically-appropriate alternative ("may be fit with adjustments"/phased return / a short certificate), and — crucially — surface the REAL driver, the hidden agenda of a workplace grievance/disciplinary, money worries and possible genuine work-related stress/low mood, which IS a legitimate, addressable need separate from the unsupported certificate. Offer legitimate help (occupational health, phased return, stress/mood support, union/Citizens Advice signposting). The examinable skill is holding the probity line WITHOUT being defensive, dismissive or confrontational — de-escalating, exploring rather than just refusing, and keeping the therapeutic relationship intact while being honest. On assessment: a mild, mechanical, improving back strain — moving freely, no neurological or red-flag features. There is no clinical basis for a three-month total sign-off; the evidence would support, at most, a short period and/or a phased/adjusted return, not a blanket long certificate.

knowledge.guideline: DWP fit note guidance for healthcare professionals · Social Security (Medical Evidence) Regulations 1976 (as amended) · NICE NG59 (low back pain and sciatica) · GMC Good Medical Practice 2024
knowledge.summary: A fit note records your honest clinical opinion of how a condition affects work. A mild, improving mechanical back strain supports at most a short note, usually "may be fit for work" with adjustments, not three months off.

points.t: The Statement of Fitness for Work gives two options: "not fit for work" or "may be fit for work" with suggested changes (phased return, altered hours, amended duties, workplace adaptations). Employees self-certify for the first 7 days. In the first 6 months of a condition a fit note can cover up to 3 months, so the question is clinical honesty, not the legal limit.

Doctors must be honest and accurate in any certificate they sign and must not sign documents they believe to be false or misleading (GMC Good Medical Practice 2024). Signing to placate or to avoid confrontation is a probity failure.

Screen for red flags (cauda equina symptoms, fever, weight loss, history of cancer, significant trauma, progressive neurology). With none, NICE NG59 advises no routine imaging, encouragement to stay active and return to normal activity including work, and a risk-stratification tool such as STarT Back.
NICE NG59 supports return to work as part of recovery for low back pain. A "may be fit" note with lighter duties or a phased return usually serves the patient better than a long absence.

A disproportionate request often reflects something else: a workplace grievance or disciplinary, money pressure, or genuine stress and low mood. Explore it without judgement. Work-related stress or depression is a legitimate condition to assess on its own terms (NICE NG222 for depression).

Since July 2022, nurses, pharmacists, physiotherapists and occupational therapists can also certify fit notes. Employer occupational health, Acas guidance on grievance and disciplinary procedures, and Citizens Advice for money problems are the right routes for the non-medical issues.

dg.d: Open question; acknowledges the request without agreeing or arguing; explains why assessment matters.
Job demands, the grievance and disciplinary, money worries, stress, mood and sleep.
Focused remote examination on camera (movement, gait); offers face-to-face if findings are unclear.
Mechanical strain against sciatica and serious causes; considers work stress and depression as separate issues.
Asks about cauda equina symptoms, fever, weight loss, cancer history and neurology.
Mild improving mechanical back strain with no red flags; separate workplace conflict.
After open exploration, used closed questions with clear signposting to confirm specific details.
Used information already available in the notes/referral; did not re-ask what was already documented or said.

dg.t: Finishes data gathering in good time
dg.d: History, ICE, psychosocial context and red-flag screen completed by ~6–7 minutes, leaving time for explanation and a shared plan.

cm.d: "May be fit for work" with amended duties or phased return; honest refusal of three months; NICE NG59 advice to stay active.
Explores and screens stress and mood; occupational health; Acas, union and Citizens Advice signposting.
Cauda equina safety-net; review in two weeks; honest documentation of assessment and rationale.

cm.t: Uses psychosocial information in the plan
cm.d: Tailored the plan to the patient’s circumstances, beliefs and practical barriers rather than giving a generic plan.

cm.t: Shares risks and safety of options
cm.d: Explained the benefits and risks of the options clearly, as concrete terms or numbers where possible.
Acknowledged autonomy, capacity, confidentiality, safeguarding and any fitness-to-drive/work or duty-of-care implications relevant to this case.
Moved efficiently through the consultation so all key areas were covered within the time without getting stuck.

ro.d: Picked up the mismatch between the request and an improving back, and asked what else was going on.
Idea (entitled to a note); concern (disciplinary and bills); expectation (three months, no questions).
Warm, non-judgmental tone; put the patient at ease and showed respect for their perspective.
Opened broadly and let the patient tell their story before narrowing down.
When a cue was offered, stopped and explored the specific concern rather than reassuring superficially and moving on.
Active listening throughout — reflecting, pausing, not interrupting — interested in the patient as a person.
Told the patient why a question, examination or test was being done — transparent reasoning throughout.
Explained the working diagnosis or analysis in plain language the patient could understand.

ro.t: Shares and uses ICE in the plan
ro.d: Addressed the patient’s specific concern — Underneath: the disciplinary hearing, losing your job and money — directly within the plan, rather than noting it and moving on.
Checked understanding, offered written/follow-up support, asked if anything else was on their mind, agreed next steps.
Clear agenda set early, logical flow from data gathering to management. Did not jump to a plan before gathering enough information.
Explained clinical terms in plain English, or defined them immediately; checked the patient was following.
Noticed and responded to emotional and verbal cues rather than continuing a fixed clinical script.

model.text: Hello Mr Dobbs, thanks for joining. I can see you want to talk about your back and some time off work. Tell me what's been happening.
model.why: Open question that acknowledges his request

model.text: Right, doc, I just need you to sign me off for three months with my back. It's killing me. I don't need an examination or twenty questions. My mate's GP does it no problem.
I can hear you're fed up, and I do want to help. Anything I put on a fit note has to be based on what I find, so I need to understand what's going on. It won't take long. Is that fair?
model.why: Stays calm, explains why assessment is needed, seeks agreement

model.text: (sighs) Go on then.
When did it start, and what were you doing?
Lifting at work. It was bad at first. It's easing a bit, to be fair.
Any pain, pins and needles or weakness down the legs? Any numbness around your bottom or between your legs, or trouble passing water or controlling your bowels?
model.why: Screens for sciatica and cauda equina

model.text: No, none of that.
Any fevers, weight loss, or a history of cancer?
No.
Could you stand back from the camera for me? Bend forward as far as is comfortable, then lean back and to each side. Now walk across the room.
(moves freely, slight stiffness on bending) There. It's stiff, but I can do it.
Thank you. That's reassuring. You're moving well, there's nothing to suggest anything serious, and it sounds like a muscle strain that's already improving.
Can I ask something? Three months is a long time off for a back that's getting better. I get the sense there might be more going on. Is something making work hard at the moment?
(pause) There's a grievance going on. They've started a disciplinary. I can't face walking back in there.
Thank you for telling me. That sounds really stressful. How's it affecting you, in yourself?
model.why: Validates and opens the psychosocial picture

model.text: It's doing my head in. And if I lose this job, I don't know how I'll pay the bills.
How's your mood been, and your sleep? Have things ever felt so bad you've thought about harming yourself?
model.why: Screens for depression and risk, since stress may be a genuine condition

model.text: Nothing like that. Just stressed and angry.

That makes much more sense of today, and I'm glad you've told me. I need to be straight with you about the note. A fit note is my honest medical opinion of how a condition affects your work. For a back strain that's improving, I can't honestly sign three months off. I'd be putting my name to something that isn't true.
model.why: Declines the unsupported certificate with a clear, honest reason

model.text: So you're not going to help me.

I am going to help, just not in that way. What I can do, honestly, is a note that says you may be fit for work with changes: lighter duties and no heavy lifting for a few weeks. People with back strains usually recover faster staying active and at work.
And the disciplinary? Lighter duties won't fix that.

You're right, and a sick note wouldn't fix it either. It would only put it off. The grievance needs sorting properly. Acas and Citizens Advice can explain your rights and help with money worries, and if you're in a union they can support you at meetings.
model.why: Separates the work dispute from the medical question and signposts

model.text: If the stress starts to affect your sleep, mood or ability to function, that's a real health problem and I'd assess it properly, with support or a note if it's genuinely needed. I'd also suggest occupational health, if your work has it. Does that feel like a fair plan?
model.why: Leaves room for genuine stress and shares the plan

model.text: I suppose. I thought you'd just refuse and that'd be it.

No. The three months wasn't the right answer, but you came with a real problem and I want to help with that. For the back, keep moving, use simple painkillers if you need them, and avoid heavy lifting for now.
model.why: Holds the line kindly and gives practical back advice

model.text: If you develop numbness between your legs, trouble passing urine or controlling your bowels, or weakness in your legs, that's an emergency: go straight to A&E. Otherwise, book in with me in two weeks and we'll see how the back and the work situation are going.
model.why: Cauda equina safety-net and defined follow-up

model.text: Alright.
Just to check we're on the same page: what are you going to take away from today?
Lighter duties note, keep moving, ring Acas about the grievance, come back in two weeks, and A&E if I get numbness or waterworks trouble.
Spot on. I'll document what we found and why the note says what it does. Thanks for being open with me.
model.why: Documents honestly and ends on a respectful note

social.t: Grievance and disciplinary processes are a common, hidden driver of sickness certification requests. Avoiding them rarely helps and can worsen the outcome.
Fear of losing income shapes behaviour. Statutory Sick Pay is paid by the employer; Citizens Advice and debt advice services can help with money worries.

legal.t: Self-certification for the first 7 days; a fit note can cover up to 3 months in the first 6 months of a condition (Social Security (Medical Evidence) Regulations 1976, as amended). Suggested adjustments are advice; the employer decides whether it can make them.
Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures sets out the process; a union representative or companion can accompany him to hearings.

professional.t: GMC Good Medical Practice 2024: be honest and trustworthy in documents, and do not sign anything you believe to be false or misleading. Document findings and the reasons for the note issued.
Stay calm and courteous; set limits if behaviour becomes abusive. Follow practice policy on unacceptable behaviour, but do not let pressure change clinical judgement.

community.t: Acas helpline for workplace disputes; trade union if a member; Citizens Advice for employment and money advice; NHS Talking Therapies if stress or low mood develops; employer occupational health.

redFlags: Saddle anaesthesia, bladder or bowel dysfunction, bilateral leg symptoms: suspected cauda equina, emergency referral
Fever, weight loss, history of cancer, night pain, significant trauma
Progressive leg weakness or neurological deficit
psychosocial: Grievance and disciplinary he is avoiding
Money worries and fear of job loss; stress, mood and sleep
ice: Idea: "I'm entitled to three months off; the GP should just sign it."
Concern: facing the disciplinary; paying the bills
Expectation: a three-month note with no questions

playbook.diagnosis: "You're moving well, there are no worrying signs, and this is a muscle strain that's already getting better."
playbook.diagnosisLay: "Think of it like a sprained ankle in your back. It's sore and stiff, but gentle movement helps it heal faster than rest."

management.reflectIce: "It sounds like the thing that's really weighing on you is the disciplinary and the money, more than the back. That's something we can actually help with."
management.psychosocial: Separate the medical question from the workplace one. Signpost Acas, union and Citizens Advice for the dispute and finances; leave the door open to assess genuine stress.
sharedPlan: Fit note: "may be fit for work" with amended duties, no heavy lifting, for a short period
Stay active; simple analgesia; no imaging (NICE NG59)
Occupational health via employer; Acas, union and Citizens Advice
Assess stress and mood if they develop; review in two weeks
safetyNet: Numbness between the legs, bladder or bowel problems, leg weakness: A&E immediately
Worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm: contact the practice or 111

pitfalls.intro: This station tests probity and relationship skills under pressure. Candidates fail by giving in, by refusing without exploring, or by getting into an argument.

items.fail: Signing three months, or a "compromise" month, to end the confrontation.
items.why: A fit note must reflect your honest assessment (GMC Good Medical Practice 2024). An unsupported certificate is a probity failure however it is negotiated.
items.fix: "The note has to match what I find. Here's what I can honestly put."

items.fail: Refusing without examining or screening for red flags.
items.why: The decision must rest on assessment, and cauda equina must not be missed.
items.fix: Ask the red-flag questions and watch him move on camera; offer face-to-face if uncertain.

items.fail: Arguing, lecturing about benefit fraud, or accusing him of malingering.
items.why: Confrontation escalates aggression and ends disclosure; the grievance never surfaces.
items.fix: Curiosity instead of accusation: "Is something else making work hard at the moment?"

items.fail: Declining the note and stopping there, with no alternative.
items.why: The "may be fit" option and signposting are the management plan; a bare refusal scores little.
items.fix: Offer amended duties or a phased return, plus Acas, union, Citizens Advice and occupational health.

items.fail: Ignoring the stress because the back request was unsupported.
items.why: Genuine work-related stress or depression is a legitimate condition that deserves assessment.
items.fix: Screen mood and sleep, and say you would assess stress properly if it is affecting his health.

items.fail: Poor time use: ten minutes of arguing about the note, no safety-net.
items.why: "Poor time management" and non-specific safety-netting are common failing feedback.
items.fix: Be explaining the honest note by minute 6; name cauda equina symptoms before closing.

items.fail: Failing to document the findings and the reason for the note.
items.why: Clear records protect the patient and you if the certificate is later questioned.
items.fix: Say you will record the assessment and rationale, and do it.

timeMap.d: He demands three months with no questions. Stay calm; explain why you need to assess and ask for his agreement.
Onset, trajectory, sciatica, cauda equina, systemic red flags. Watch him move on camera.
"Three months is a long time for a back that's improving. Is something else going on?" Grievance, money, mood.
Decline three months with a clear reason. Offer "may be fit" with amended duties. Signpost Acas, union, Citizens Advice, OH.
Cauda equina symptoms named. Review in two weeks. Teach-back. Document the assessment.

wordPics.fail: Signs three months to avoid conflict, or refuses flatly without examining or exploring; argues with him; never finds out about the grievance; no safety-net.
wordPics.pass: Assesses the back and excludes red flags; declines the three-month note with a clear reason; offers a "may be fit" note with adjustments; asks about work; safety-nets for cauda equina.
wordPics.exc: All of the above, plus: de-escalates early by seeking agreement; explores the mismatch without accusing; surfaces the grievance and money worries; screens mood; separates the workplace problem from the medical one and signposts specifically; leaves the door open for genuine stress; he ends the consultation feeling helped rather than refused.

avoid.dont: "I'm not signing that. Your back's fine."
avoid.instead: "I can't honestly sign three months for a back that's improving, but I can do a note for lighter duties, and I'd like to help with what's really going on."
avoid.why: A flat refusal escalates conflict and loses the Relating domain.

avoid.dont: "Okay, I'll do a month and we'll see."
avoid.instead: "The note has to match what I find. Here's what I can honestly offer."
avoid.why: A compromise certificate that the findings don't support is still dishonest.

avoid.dont: "Are you just trying to avoid work?"
avoid.instead: "Three months is a long time for a back that's settling. Is something else making work hard?"
avoid.why: Accusation shuts down disclosure; curiosity opens it.

SCA_KNOWLEDGE.summary: A fit note records your honest clinical opinion of how a condition affects work. A mild, improving mechanical back strain supports at most a short note, usually "may be fit for work" with adjustments, not three months off.

points.t: The Statement of Fitness for Work gives two options: "not fit for work" or "may be fit for work" with suggested changes (phased return, altered hours, amended duties, workplace adaptations). Employees self-certify for the first 7 days. In the first 6 months of a condition a fit note can cover up to 3 months, so the question is clinical honesty, not the legal limit.

Doctors must be honest and accurate in any certificate they sign and must not sign documents they believe to be false or misleading (GMC Good Medical Practice 2024). Signing to placate or to avoid confrontation is a probity failure.

Screen for red flags (cauda equina symptoms, fever, weight loss, history of cancer, significant trauma, progressive neurology). With none, NICE NG59 advises no routine imaging, encouragement to stay active and return to normal activity including work, and a risk-stratification tool such as STarT Back.
NICE NG59 supports return to work as part of recovery for low back pain. A "may be fit" note with lighter duties or a phased return usually serves the patient better than a long absence.

A disproportionate request often reflects something else: a workplace grievance or disciplinary, money pressure, or genuine stress and low mood. Explore it without judgement. Work-related stress or depression is a legitimate condition to assess on its own terms (NICE NG222 for depression).

Since July 2022, nurses, pharmacists, physiotherapists and occupational therapists can also certify fit notes. Employer occupational health, Acas guidance on grievance and disciplinary procedures, and Citizens Advice for money problems are the right routes for the non-medical issues.

SCA_SC_TASKS.d: Open question; acknowledges the request without agreeing or arguing; explains why assessment matters.
Job demands, the grievance and disciplinary, money worries, stress, mood and sleep.
Picked up the mismatch between the request and an improving back, and asked what else was going on.
Idea (entitled to a note); concern (disciplinary and bills); expectation (three months, no questions).
Focused remote examination on camera (movement, gait); offers face-to-face if findings are unclear.
Mechanical strain against sciatica and serious causes; considers work stress and depression as separate issues.
Asks about cauda equina symptoms, fever, weight loss, cancer history and neurology.
Mild improving mechanical back strain with no red flags; separate workplace conflict.
"May be fit for work" with amended duties or phased return; honest refusal of three months; NICE NG59 advice to stay active.
Explores and screens stress and mood; occupational health; Acas, union and Citizens Advice signposting.
Cauda equina safety-net; review in two weeks; honest documentation of assessment and rationale.

social.t: Grievance and disciplinary processes are a common, hidden driver of sickness certification requests. Avoiding them rarely helps and can worsen the outcome.
Fear of losing income shapes behaviour. Statutory Sick Pay is paid by the employer; Citizens Advice and debt advice services can help with money worries.

legal.t: Self-certification for the first 7 days; a fit note can cover up to 3 months in the first 6 months of a condition (Social Security (Medical Evidence) Regulations 1976, as amended). Suggested adjustments are advice; the employer decides whether it can make them.
Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures sets out the process; a union representative or companion can accompany him to hearings.

professional.t: GMC Good Medical Practice 2024: be honest and trustworthy in documents, and do not sign anything you believe to be false or misleading. Document findings and the reasons for the note issued.
Stay calm and courteous; set limits if behaviour becomes abusive. Follow practice policy on unacceptable behaviour, but do not let pressure change clinical judgement.

community.t: Acas helpline for workplace disputes; trade union if a member; Citizens Advice for employment and money advice; NHS Talking Therapies if stress or low mood develops; employer occupational health.

redFlags: Saddle anaesthesia, bladder or bowel dysfunction, bilateral leg symptoms: suspected cauda equina, emergency referral
Fever, weight loss, history of cancer, night pain, significant trauma
Progressive leg weakness or neurological deficit
psychosocial: Grievance and disciplinary he is avoiding
Money worries and fear of job loss; stress, mood and sleep
ice: Idea: "I'm entitled to three months off; the GP should just sign it."
Concern: facing the disciplinary; paying the bills
Expectation: a three-month note with no questions

SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosis: "You're moving well, there are no worrying signs, and this is a muscle strain that's already getting better."
SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosisLay: "Think of it like a sprained ankle in your back. It's sore and stiff, but gentle movement helps it heal faster than rest."

management.reflectIce: "It sounds like the thing that's really weighing on you is the disciplinary and the money, more than the back. That's something we can actually help with."
management.psychosocial: Separate the medical question from the workplace one. Signpost Acas, union and Citizens Advice for the dispute and finances; leave the door open to assess genuine stress.
sharedPlan: Fit note: "may be fit for work" with amended duties, no heavy lifting, for a short period
Stay active; simple analgesia; no imaging (NICE NG59)
Occupational health via employer; Acas, union and Citizens Advice
Assess stress and mood if they develop; review in two weeks
safetyNet: Numbness between the legs, bladder or bowel problems, leg weakness: A&E immediately
Worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm: contact the practice or 111

SCA_PITFALLS.intro: This station tests probity and relationship skills under pressure. Candidates fail by giving in, by refusing without exploring, or by getting into an argument.

items.fail: Signing three months, or a "compromise" month, to end the confrontation.
items.why: A fit note must reflect your honest assessment (GMC Good Medical Practice 2024). An unsupported certificate is a probity failure however it is negotiated.
items.fix: "The note has to match what I find. Here's what I can honestly put."

items.fail: Refusing without examining or screening for red flags.
items.why: The decision must rest on assessment, and cauda equina must not be missed.
items.fix: Ask the red-flag questions and watch him move on camera; offer face-to-face if uncertain.

items.fail: Arguing, lecturing about benefit fraud, or accusing him of malingering.
items.why: Confrontation escalates aggression and ends disclosure; the grievance never surfaces.
items.fix: Curiosity instead of accusation: "Is something else making work hard at the moment?"

items.fail: Declining the note and stopping there, with no alternative.
items.why: The "may be fit" option and signposting are the management plan; a bare refusal scores little.
items.fix: Offer amended duties or a phased return, plus Acas, union, Citizens Advice and occupational health.

items.fail: Ignoring the stress because the back request was unsupported.
items.why: Genuine work-related stress or depression is a legitimate condition that deserves assessment.
items.fix: Screen mood and sleep, and say you would assess stress properly if it is affecting his health.

items.fail: Poor time use: ten minutes of arguing about the note, no safety-net.
items.why: "Poor time management" and non-specific safety-netting are common failing feedback.
items.fix: Be explaining the honest note by minute 6; name cauda equina symptoms before closing.

items.fail: Failing to document the findings and the reason for the note.
items.why: Clear records protect the patient and you if the certificate is later questioned.
items.fix: Say you will record the assessment and rationale, and do it.
